analyst_view.overall: Second-placed Roma (30 points, unbeaten, four straight league wins with 17 goals) host Monza, 14th with 10 points, who ended a four-game losing run by beating Fiorentina 3-0 but have only one point away from home. Roma drew 2-2 at PSG on Wednesday and Gasperini said several players finished very tired; La Gazzetta expects several changes, mostly in defence and on the right (Ghilardi, Lulli), with Dybala, Malen and Soule fresh to start after coming off the bench in Paris. Pellegrini and Rensch are out (counted by the numbers). Monza's Ivan Juric, Roma coach for a short spell in 2024, has Folorunsho, Ngonge and Ciurria still being assessed rather than ruled out, and Pessina is back from knee surgery. Referee Giuseppe Collu (4.3 cards a game) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals, already boosted by Roma's 21 goals in their last six. I said -5% before when Monza's Folorunsho and Ngonge looked out; they are now only doubts, so I cut the lean to -3%, about 3.5, for Roma's tired legs and a reshuffled defence three days after Paris. Dybala, Malen and Soule starting fresh up front keeps it small.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners, already lifting Roma for their 36 corners in six and trimming Monza for their 20. Juric's Monza play a 3-4-2-1 with wing-backs and defend deep away from home, which feeds Roma's corners, but the numbers already see that pattern; I stay at about 9.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards, raised about 13% for referee Giuseppe Collu (4.3 a game) and trimmed for both sides' slightly quiet recent records. Juric's return to the Olimpico adds a little edge, but no suspensions or new tensions show up in the previews, so I stay at about 4.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.3 shots, already raising Roma by 12% for their 101 shots in six. Gasperini said several players came off very tired in Paris and he will change part of the team, and Monza's Ngonge, Folorunsho and Ciurria are all doubts, so I lean slightly lower, about 27.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.0 shots on target, already lifted strongly for Roma's 43 on target in six (+18%). With fatigue after Paris and Monza's attacking doubts, I lean a little lower, about 10.6; Varela, the league's top scorer, keeps Monza's share from falling far.
